findings.location: Decoded input, RAW row value (687,1002)-(700,1016), directly under SELECTOR value `0x1a2b3c4d` (687,975)
findings.finding: New this round. RAW now renders a bare em dash at the 14px value rung, in the row immediately beneath a row that renders four bytes of the very payload the dash denies — a selector IS the first bytes of the call data, so the pair reads as a contradiction rather than as one emptiness test. It also gives the page a third vocabulary for absence in three sections: a worded chip (AGE `No timestamp published`), worded sentences (Events, Internal calls, State changes), and now a glyph with no words at all, whose explanation is 45px below it in a separate card. Either label the row `ARGUMENTS`, or set RAW to the selector bytes it is a prefix of.

findings.location: Overview grid, value column: TYPE `public` (687,965) versus CANONICAL `Yes` (687,1046) and FINALITY `Pending` (687,1084)
findings.finding: Carried and re-verified by measurement. The value column runs at two type rungs for one class of data: `public` is plain 14px mono (x-height 7px, ascender 10px), while `Yes` and `Pending` are 12px letterspaced mono (x-height 6px) inside a bordered chip — the same rung as the 12px uppercase label column opposite them. All three are short categorical enums, so the split does not track data type and a reader cannot infer what the chip means. The chip is also the page's smallest type, applied to values, next to labels of the same size.

findings.location: Overview grid, AGE row value (690,1000)-(855,1018)
findings.finding: Carried and strengthened. `No timestamp published` — 22 characters of English, the grid's only honest-absence statement — is set at 12px letterspaced monospace inside the chip the page reserves for one-word machine tokens, making it the smallest type on a 2840px page and two rungs below the values it sits among. Letterspaced mono makes a sentence read as a value the chain emitted, which is the opposite of what the row exists to say. It should be set unchipped in the body face at the value rung.

findings.location: section rules: full-width hairlines at y=716, 1314, 1675 and 2290, above Overview (506,747), Decoded input (506,1345) and Raw (506,2321); no rule above Internal calls (506,1885) or State changes (506,2064)
findings.finding: Carried and re-verified. All six section headings are identical — 17px cap height, bold, same colour — so the hairline is the only heading-level signal on the page, and it falls above four of six peers. The resulting groups are {Overview}, {Decoded input}, {Events, Internal calls, State changes}, {Raw}: three sections read as one block whose members look exactly like the three that stand alone. The grouping also cuts against the page's own copy, which says Events comes from the receipt while the two beneath it come from the trace. With eight sections in one scroll the heading treatment has to be navigable without reading; here it groups without saying so.

findings.location: hero (506,200)-(1150,310) versus Overview grid FINALITY row (687,1084)
findings.finding: Carried. The expectation block places the finality badge in the hero; the hero carries only the `Succeeded` status badge, the truncated hash and the copy box. Finality appears nine rows down as `Pending`, at the 12px chip rung shared with CANONICAL, so a reader who takes the hero and the primary action — the top 440px — sees an unqualified success and no signal that the transaction is not yet final. Recorded P2 and not P1 because the badge is present, labelled and legible: its position in the hierarchy is wrong, not the information.

findings.location: hero H1 `0x27a6…9a6c` (506,236)-(712,259) against the section headings, e.g. Overview (506,747)-(600,763)
findings.finding: Downgraded from P2 after measurement. The H1's figure height is 24px against the headings' 17px cap height — a 1.41x step that does read as two levels, so last round's `effectively one level` no longer holds. What remains is a weight inversion: the H1's stems measure 3px on a 24px glyph (0.125) while the headings' measure 3-4px on a 17px cap (0.21), so the single level-one title is the lightest relative stroke on the page and the six repeated level-two headings are the heaviest. Size and weight still pull in opposite directions; the step now survives it.

findings.location: Overview grid, COST · MANA row value (687,1185)-(960,1205)
findings.finding: Downgraded from P2. `42000  /  100000 mana (FeeJuice)` sets two quantities joined by a bare slash with no sub-label distinguishing usage from limit, and neither figure is grouped, so two five- and six-digit magnitudes must be compared digit by digit. The used/limit slash is a widely-read explorer idiom and the figures are correctly tabular mono with the unit dropped to the proportional muted face, so this is a refinement rather than a failure. Note also that the round's label humanisation is not visible here: the only cost label on this view is `COST · MANA` and the label column is uppercase, so a humanised source string would still render `COST · TRANSACTION FEE`.

findings.location: footer disclosure line (506,2740)-(1416,2780)
findings.finding: Carried. The disclosure sets roughly 130 characters on its first line across a 920px column, about double the ~70-character measure the provenance sentences (687,825), the trace note (528,465) and the three section notes hold to. Two lines, so it is readable; it is the one place on the page where prose is set to its container rather than to a measure.

findings.location: copy affordance, hero (506,276)-(925,308) and the `click to select` caption at (935,288)
findings.finding: Carried. The full hash sits at ~16px monospace, regular weight, on a white fill inside a hairline rounded border, with the gesture named by a 13px grey caption set outside the box. Nothing in the weight or the caption's prominence says the box is pressable; it reads as a read-only field displaying the value. A caption in the label register, or the value at control weight, would resolve it.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) code block, lines at y=2375, 2398, 2423, 2446, 2467, 2490
findings.finding: Carried and measured. Line pitch is 23px on ~14px monospace (~1.64), the body-prose line-height applied to code, while one indent level is two spaces — about 17px. The lines therefore sit further apart than the indentation is wide, so the nesting reads weaker than it is in the page's only preformatted region. A pitch near 20px would let the indent structure carry.

findings.location: page right edge — trace card (x504-1203, y359-610), decoded-input note (x504-1203, y1479-1572), Events note (y1756-1828), Internal calls note (y1935-2007), State changes note (y2114-2187), against the section rules at y716/1314/1675/2290, both facts grids (y779-1213, y1377-1451), the raw <pre> (y2357-2519), the nav resolver field and the footer content — all of which end at x=1415
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1 and re-measured to the pixel: the column has two right edges 212px apart, alternating down the whole scroll. Every bordered panel carrying prose stops at x=1203; every rule, grid, the raw block and both pieces of site chrome run to x=1415. The left edges agree exactly at x=504, so the reader cannot read the 1203 edge as a narrower measure — it reads as a container that failed to fill. The four section rules make it worst: each is a 912px hairline drawn straight across a stack whose visible card edges stop 212px short of it.

findings.location: section headings — Overview (baseline y764, grid top y779), Decoded input (y1362 / y1377), Raw (chain-native) (y2337 / y2357) versus Events (y1723 / y1756), Internal calls (y1902 / y1935), State changes (y2081 / y2114)
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1: one relationship is set at three values on one page. Heading baseline to the top of its first content is 15px where that content is a facts grid, 20px where it is the raw <pre>, and 33px where it is a notice card. The gap tracks the component that follows rather than the heading, so the same heading level binds tightly to a grid and loosely to a card, and the six sections do not read as peers. Pick one value — 24px would sit on the scale the rest of the page uses (30px rule-to-heading, 56px card-to-heading, ~102px section-to-section).

findings.location: hero — `Succeeded` badge at x724-833, y232-262 — versus the Overview grid's FINALITY row, `Pending` badge at x680-750, y1067-1100
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1 and re-measured: 837px of vertical separation, with eight grid rows between them. Status and finality are one judgement about whether this transaction counts, and proximity here says they are unrelated. §7.2 places the finality badge in the hero beside the status; the hero has room — the h1 plus badge end at x=833 and the row is empty to x=1415. Moving `Pending` beside `Succeeded` also removes the page's only badge pair separated by more than the viewport height.

findings.location: Overview grid, DATA row — the provenance paragraph occupying y817-914, text ink x529-1121, against the label column fill x505-665 and the nine value cells whose text starts at x=690
findings.finding: New. The provenance sentences start at x=529 — the label column's own text edge — while every value in both grids starts at x=690, so the longest passage on the page is the one item in the grid that does not sit in the value column. Because the paragraph spans the full 912px, it also punches a 97px white gap (y817-914) through the label column's continuous grey band, which otherwise runs unbroken from y780 to y1213; a reader scanning the label column hits a hole four rows from the top. Either indent the paragraph to x=690 so it belongs to the DATA row's value cell, or drop the label-column fill for the whole DATA group so the break is deliberate rather than a leak.

findings.location: `Internal calls` heading (cap top y1885) between the Events card ending y1828 and its own card starting y1935; `State changes` heading (cap top y2063) between the Internal calls card ending y2007 and its own card starting y2114
findings.finding: New. Both headings are equidistant from the section above and the content below — 57px above / 50px below, and 56px / 51px — which is the failure §5 A2 names verbatim. Neither heading has a rule above it (Overview, Decoded input, Events and Raw all do), so spacing is the only grouping signal available and it is not being used: at a glance the heading reads as trailing the previous card as readily as introducing its own. Cutting the below-gap to the 24-33px band the other four sections use, or widening the above-gap toward the ~102px section rhythm, would settle it.

findings.location: Overview grid, value column — badge borders at x=680 (DATA y798, AGE y1007, CANONICAL y1045, FINALITY y1083) versus plain value text at x=690 (BLOCK, TYPE, FEE PAYER, TARGET, COST · MANA)
findings.finding: Carried from vd9-r1 and worth accepting rather than fixing. The value column's visible left edge alternates between x=680 and x=690 over nine rows. It is defensible: each badge's own text begins at x=689-691, so the offset is a deliberate negative inset that makes the badge's letters align with the plain values, which is the more important edge. Recording it so the next reviewer does not re-derive it as a defect.

findings.location: trace card, the inner hairline at y548 (x529-1179) between the three-line explanation (ink ending y519) and the line `Internal calls and state changes come from the execution trace.` (ink starting y566)
findings.finding: New. The divider is not centred in the space it divides: roughly 26px of clearance above it and 13px below, once line boxes rather than ink are accounted for. It therefore reads as attached to the sentence beneath it rather than as a separator between two zones of one card, which is at odds with the card's otherwise symmetric 25/24px horizontal and 28px vertical padding.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) block, x504-1415, y2357-2519 — text ink x531-1040, y2375-2503
findings.finding: New. The one preformatted region on the page uses 27px of horizontal padding against roughly 16-18px vertical, so its content sits noticeably closer to the top and bottom edges than to the left. Every other bordered surface on the page is padded evenly (notice cards 24/24 with 19px ink inset; facts-grid cells 25px). Equalising to 24px would bring the block onto the same inset as its neighbours.

findings.location: hero — h1 ink ends x711, `Succeeded` badge border starts x724; trace card — `Generate trace` button ends x679, `On demand` chip border starts x696
findings.finding: Carried from vd9-r1. The page's two control-plus-chip pairs use different gaps, 13px and 17px, 150px apart vertically. Both pairs are otherwise well set — the badge's bottom edge y262 lands on the h1 baseline, and the chip's vertical centre y410 matches the button's y411 — so a single 16px gap would finish them.

findings.location: Overview grid, value cells of the Age, Canonical and Finality rows
findings.finding: One chip token — fill #F3F3F3, border #C8C8C8, text #565656 — carries three unrelated meanings: an absent datum ("No timestamp published"), an affirmative fact ("Yes") and an in-progress state ("Pending"). The palette demonstrably has the tones to separate them: the hero's Succeeded chip is #DCFCE7 / #16A34A / #166534 and the Data badge is #DBEAFE / #2563EB / #1E40AF. Canonical: Yes is a confirmed positive rendered in the same grey as a missing value, so the grid's only three status cells are indistinguishable by colour and must all be read. Unchanged since round 1.

findings.location: Hero action card — Generate trace button (x 529-679) and the On demand chip (x 696-797)
findings.finding: Indigo #4F46E5 (hue 243, L 59%) and blue #2563EB (hue 221, L 53%) sit 16px edge to edge, 22 degrees and 6 lightness points apart. Last round measured 14px; the gap moved by 2px and the hue relationship did not change, so the finding stands. The chip compounds it: white fill, 1px saturated #2563EB border, #1E40AF label — the only outline pill on a page whose other three chips (Succeeded, Data, the grey trio) are all tinted-fill. Outline-pill-beside-filled-button is the standard secondary-button pattern, so a non-interactive state label reads as the second half of a button pair, and the indigo/blue distinction the design relies on is not perceivable at that separation.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) block, y 2353-2524; also the hero hash chip and the Overview grid cell borders
findings.finding: The border token family sits below the 3:1 non-text floor on every surface it is used on, and worst where it carries the most load. The Raw block is the only container on the page with no fill — it is #ECECEB, identical to the canvas — so a 1px #A2A2A2 hairline at 2.16:1 is the sole thing containing the largest, densest region on the page. Unchanged since round 1, to the second decimal. The same #A2A2A2 reaches only 2.55:1 on the white note panels, the hero hash chip's #C8C8C8 boundary is 1.67:1 on white despite being the click-to-select affordance, and the grid's internal separators are the same 1.67:1. Three container treatments coexist: the hero card (white, shadow, no border), the notes and grid (white, hairline, no shadow) and Raw (no fill, hairline).

findings.location: Overview grid, Data row — the Synthetic demo data badge
findings.finding: The badge the spec calls for "in the neutral tone" renders in the accent-blue family: fill #DBEAFE, border #2563EB, text #1E40AF. That is not this page's neutral tone — grey #F3F3F3 / #565656 is, and finding 1 shows it being spent on three rows that do not need it. The consequence is that the one element graded as content rather than decoration wears the same #2563EB as the hero's trace-state chip and sits one hue step from the primary action's #4F46E5, so a caveat about data provenance is drawn with accent weight and reads as a highlight. Contrast is fine (7.15:1); the tone assignment is the problem.

findings.location: Decoded input grid, RAW row value cell
findings.finding: New this round as a consequence of change (a). The em dash is drawn in #242424, the same full-emphasis value colour as the real selector directly above it, so "no payload" and "0x1a2b3c4d" carry identical weight. The page already has a muted treatment for absence — the Age row's #565656 chip — so it now states absence two ways. Setting the dash to #565656 would align it.

findings.location: Site nav resolver field, and the Overview / Decoded input grids' label column
findings.finding: #DDDDDD is both the fill of the page's only text input and the fill of every static label cell, and both carry a grey hairline. The one editable surface on the page is therefore the same colour as a read-only column, distinguished only by the placeholder's wording.

findings.location: Footer, right column — the heart in "Built with ♥ by Metacraft Labs"
findings.finding: The heart is #4F46E5, the same token as the three real links beside it, while the sentence around it is #484848. A reader scanning that column for links sees four indigo marks, one of which is decorative and not interactive.

findings.location: hero status badge at (725-835, y 232-262); AGE row y 989-1027 and FINALITY row y 1064-1102 in the Overview grid
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1 and re-measured: the hero carries status alone. `Succeeded` sits at y=247; the age statement is 761px below it and the `Pending` finality badge 836px below it, both as grid rows. New this round: at 1920x1080 the fold falls at y=1080, which cuts the FINALITY row (1064-1102) in half, so the one fact that qualifies a green `Succeeded` is clipped at exactly the fold rather than merely below it. The information is present, so this is placement, not breakage — but the hero has 480px of unused width at x>1203 to carry both.

findings.location: Overview grid, x 503-1416, y 780-1214; Decoded input grid y 1375-1450; Raw block y 2344-2549
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1: one label/value pair per 913px row at a 1920px viewport. The longest value on the page, the FEE PAYER hash at y=1195, ends at x=1043, so 373px — 40.9% — is empty on all nine rows, and the grid still costs 434px of scroll. The Raw JSON block repeats the ratio exactly (longest line ends x=1044). The page is now 2840px, 2.63 viewport heights, to deliver nine grid rows, five sentences and six lines of JSON, and the whole column is 913px of a 1920px viewport. Two pairs per row, or a narrower column with the freed width used, would remove roughly 200px of scroll without dropping anything.

findings.location: Events heading y=1704 through the State changes card ending y=2187
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1 (475px reported there; 483px now, the 8px being downstream drift from the longer ABI note). Three headings and three identically shaped 700px cards spend 483px — 45% of a 1080px viewport — on 53 words: 19 in Events, 17 in Internal calls, 17 in State changes. My r1 count of 46 was low; correcting it makes the ratio worse, not better. The trace card already prints `Internal calls and state changes come from the execution trace.` at y=571, and the two lower cards restate it split in two. The identical card shape also makes the run read as one block rather than three sections.

findings.location: right edges: Overview grid, Decoded input grid and Raw block end at x=1416; trace card, ABI note and the three statement cards end at x=1203
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1: the column has two right edges 213px apart, alternating down the page. The cost is not only alignment — the ABI note at y 1475-1573 wraps to three lines against a 700px measure while the grid 25px above it runs to x=1416, so the narrower cards wrap early against unused column width.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) block, x 503-1416, y 2344-2549
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1: the one preformatted region holds six lines whose longest reaches x=1044, so 41% of the block is empty and it carries a four-key transaction object with no receipt object beside it, which the expectation asks for. There is still no visible max-height, scroll container or copy control, so at realistic volume — a real receipt is hundreds of lines — this block would run the page height past 2840px unbounded.

findings.location: Overview grid label column, x 517-664, e.g. `COST · MANA` at y=1195
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1: the labels are roughly 10px uppercase, letterspaced, in a mid grey — the smallest and lightest text on the page — and they are the only wayfinding into a nine-row grid whose rows are 38px tall. The size budget is inverted: there is generous row height to scan by and the thing being scanned is set at the floor.

findings.location: DATA row and provenance note at the head of the Overview grid, y 780-914
findings.finding: Unchanged from vd9-r1: the DATA row plus its note stand 134px tall against 38px rows, 31% of the grid's height, so every scannable fact begins 134px into a grid the reader entered under the heading `Overview`. The note's own measure also stops at x=1121, leaving 295px of the row empty. A secondary size under the badge would keep the claim and return the row rhythm at the grid's head.

findings.location: Decoded input grid, RAW row, value at x 688-698, y 1414-1450
findings.finding: New, and a consequence of change (a). Replacing `0x` with `—` is the honest call — `0x` asserted a zero-length payload the tree does not have — but it leaves a 10px glyph occupying a 913px x 36px row, 98.9% empty, and it is the third idiom this page uses for the same idea within 570px of scroll: the AGE row states absence as a bordered chip reading `No timestamp published` (y=1008), the RAW row as a bare em dash, and the Events/Internal calls/State changes sections as prose cards. The AGE chip is the strongest of the three and is the page's own pattern; the em dash carries none of its specificity and relies on the note 25px below to do the explaining.

findings.location: Decoded input section, heading y=1329 through the note card ending y=1573
findings.finding: New, and a consequence of change (c). The section now spends 244px of scroll to report an eight-character selector: a 46px heading, a two-row 75px grid holding `0x1a2b3c4d` and an em dash, and a 98px three-line note. The note itself grew to 38 words and accounts for the page going from 2818px to 2840px. Its last clause, `An ABI would not help, and BlockTracer cannot yet be given one in any case.`, states two overlapping facts where one would do; the honesty gain over the previous promise is real, but it was bought with a line of scroll rather than by rewriting the sentence.

findings.location: hero, beside the H1 hash `0x27a6…9a6c`
findings.finding: The expected element places the finality badge in the hero; only the green `Succeeded` status badge is there. Finality renders as `Pending` in row six of the Overview grid, roughly 800px further down. In the explorer register the hero is the at-a-glance answer, and an affirmative-toned badge standing alone there reads as settled. Move the `Pending` finality badge next to `Succeeded` so the two qualify each other.

findings.location: section headings across the page body
findings.finding: The full-measure hairline section rule is applied to four of six peer headings: it sits above `Overview`, `Decoded input`, `Events` and `Raw (chain-native)`, but not above `Internal calls` or `State changes`. All six headings are the same type level, so the rule marks groups that do not exist and the eight-sections-in-one-scroll navigation cue stops being trustworthy. Apply the divider to every peer heading or to none.

findings.location: Decoded input grid, RAW row versus Overview grid, AGE row
findings.finding: The same facts-grid primitive speaks two dialects for absent data. The AGE row carries a labelled chip, `No timestamp published`, which is the voice the brief asks for. The RAW row carries a bare em dash. Both mean 'the tree holds nothing here', and the em dash is the less informative of the two and the one that most resembles a rendering failure. Give RAW a `No call data` chip in the AGE row's treatment; the explanatory note below then reinforces rather than rescues it.

findings.location: Overview grid, DATA row — the `Synthetic demo data` provenance chip
findings.finding: The provenance chip is the only accent-hued chip on the page: it takes the indigo/blue hue family that the primary `Generate trace` button, the breadcrumb links and the `102:0` block link all use. Its three grid siblings (`No timestamp published`, `Yes`, `Pending`) are neutral grey and `Succeeded` is green. The label is not contradicted — blue reads informational, not affirmative — so this is not a tone failure, but the marker borrows the brand's action hue for a statement that is neither an action nor a link. A distinct neutral-informational tone outside the link hue would let it read as fact.

findings.location: Decoded input, explanatory note under the grid
findings.finding: Two copy defects in the new sentence. `This selector is not in any ABI BlockTracer holds` garden-paths — with the relative pronoun elided, `ABI BlockTracer` parses as a compound noun on first read; insert `that`. And `An ABI would not help, and BlockTracer cannot yet be given one in any case` ends weakly: `in any case` is redundant after `and`, and `yet` smuggles a roadmap promise into a statement of present fact. Suggest: `…so there are no parameters to decode. An ABI would not help here, and BlockTracer cannot be given one.`

findings.location: Overview grid, `COST · MANA` row

Either drop the resource noun from the label (`COST`, value keeps `mana`) or complete the humanisation the way `Cost · Transaction fee` was described.

findings.location: hero card note, Internal calls note, State changes note
findings.finding: One fact is stated three times in three wordings on a single scroll: the hero's spec-mandated `Internal calls and state changes come from the execution trace.`, then `Internal calls come from the execution trace. They appear here once this transaction has a recorded trace.`, then the same sentence again for state changes. The repetition is structural rather than careless, but three near-variants read as templated where the surrounding copy reads as written. Consider having the two section notes lead with what they would show rather than restating their source.

findings.location: hero card note versus footer data disclosure
findings.finding: The hero note says generating a trace `needs an account`; the footer on the same page opens `No account, no tracking`. Both are true and the account requirement is the one sanctioned path, but a reader who sees both on one page sees a contradiction and has no cue that the requirement is the exception. One clause defuses it — e.g. `it is the only thing in BlockTracer that needs an account, and nothing is computed in your browser`. Tone only; the honesty is intact.

findings.location: Hero, the line directly beneath the H1 — the bordered full-hash box (approx. x 504-920, y 278-308 in the 1920x2840 image) and the grey `click to select` label immediately to its right at approx. x 932-1025
findings.finding: The copy affordance for the full transaction hash is rendered as prose, not as a control. In the resting state there is no icon, no button and no border, fill or weight change to mark the box as interactive — the sole cue is a ~13px low-contrast grey label set outside the element it governs, which a reader scanning the hero will take for a caption rather than an instruction. It also names a smaller action than the one a block-explorer reader arrives expecting: `select`, not `copy`, so even a reader who does read it is told the page will do less for them than every competitor's hash row does. Compounding both, the container is a rounded, thin-bordered white field built to the same pattern as the resolver input in the fixed nav, so the assembly parses as a read-only text field with helper text rather than as the page's most-used action. Copying the hash is the single most-performed interaction on a transaction page and this is the page a competitor comparison lands on; every other control on the screen — `Generate trace`, the `102:0` block link, the footer links — is drawn as unambiguously actionable, which makes this one the outlier rather than the house style. This is the only MUST SHOW item on the page where present-versus-absent was a judgement call, and that is what makes it the weakest element here.

findings.location: Transaction pane, DATA provenance note, x1158-1419, y250-443

findings.location: Code pane, window note line 1, tail at x630-660, y172-184

findings.location: Transaction pane FEE PAYER (y614-670) and TARGET (y685-740); Values pane `masses` row (y672-700); Call Trace frame rows 4 and 8 (y204-215, y283-294)

findings.location: Identity bar, phase rail x958-1200, against stepping controls x370-655 and readout x880-970

findings.location: Transaction pane, rule between the DATA label row (y215-245) and the note (y250-443)

findings.location: Code pane gutter, glyph column x75-85, lines 27-32 (y255-395)

findings.location: Code pane loop rail, y95-130, x20-420

findings.location: Tabbed Call Trace / Event Log region, y62-561; last frame row ends y301, footer 'By call order. / Self cost' ends y320

findings.location: Transaction pane body, bottom fade ramp, y848-888, over the EXECUTIONS sentence (lines at y857 and y877)
findings.finding: New this round, caused by the fade. The ramp is set in pixels (~40px) rather than in line boxes, and the four pane bodies have three different line grids: 25px code rows, 25px table rows, 21.5px prose. In the Code pane this happens to land between rows - line 51 keeps a min luminance of 72 (about 7.3:1) and only the line-52 numeral is ghosted - so the fade reads as 'more rows below'. In the Transaction pane it starts mid-paragraph: 'Aztec private functions execute client-side;' at y857 holds 86, but 'only proofs, nullifiers and commitments are' at y877 runs from 118 (4.5:1) to 153 (2.85:1) across one line, so a single sentence carries three contrast levels and appears to be going pale rather than continuing. The affordance is right and worth keeping; snap the ramp's opaque stop to the last whole line box of the body so it always begins at a row boundary.

findings.location: All pane bodies, bottom edge — measured at Transaction pane y870–894 and Code pane y870–894
findings.finding: Change (a) landed but the ramp is geometrically too short to read as recession. Measured alpha: Transaction pane, the EXECUTIONS sentence's last line 'only proofs, nullifiers and commitments are' (y874-885) goes 0.81 alpha at y875 to 0.44 at y884, linear, reaching 0 at y896; base text is 86-grey on white, so contrast falls 4.54:1 to 2.05:1 ACROSS ONE LINE — a glyph's ascender is legible and its baseline is not, which reads as a smear rather than as depth. That is worse than the 2.19:1 one lens measured at wide, so the concern is not a wide-viewport artefact; at laptop it lands on the provenance/EXECUTIONS prose that brief 4 grades as content. The ramp is 24-26px against a 19px pitch in the Transaction pane and 23px in the Code listing — about 1.1-1.4 line-pitches — so at most one line is ever inside it. In the Code pane the only line inside is line 52's 9px sliver, whose realised peak opacity is 0.31: a 4px grey trace that reads as a rendering artefact, not as continuation. In the Values pane content ends at y851, 19px above the ramp, so the fade is invisible there (correct, nothing continues). Fix: ramp about 2 line-pitches, 46-50px, with the ramp's top anchored to a line boundary so two lines step down at roughly per-line-uniform alpha (about 0.7 then about 0.3). 46-50px also matches the 46px horizontal ramp already used in this same Code pane, making it one device at one scale, and costs one line of legible content rather than the three a 3-pitch ramp would cost at 900px tall.

findings.location: Call Trace tabbed region, x691-1144, y68-561
findings.finding: The queued emptiness holds, re-measured: the tabbed region is 494px of the middle column's 828px (59.7%); its last ink is the 'By call order. / Self cost' footer at y309-320; y321-559 is pure white (255,255,255 sampled every 20px) — 239px, 48.4% of the region, 51.5% of the body below the tab strip. Last round's 48.8%/48.2% therefore stands essentially unchanged, and it is layout-shaped: the split is a fixed share of the column, not a consequence of this fixture, and the Values pane below it does NOT absorb the difference — its last row ('i', ends y851) leaves 42px of slack (12.7%) before the pane border at y895. So the middle column as a whole is about 281px taller than the content it holds, and the surplus sits in the one column where neither pane can spend it. The two panes that genuinely overflow at this viewport are Code (6 of 27 visible lines clipped at the right, line 52 cut at the bottom) and Transaction (cut mid-sentence in EXECUTIONS) — both in other columns. Within this column the honest weighting is content-driven rather than 60/40: size the tabbed region to its content plus two rows and let Values take the remainder, because Values' row count grows as the user steps while trace depth here is fixed at 7 frames. The re-weighting remains a taste call; the measurement is not.

findings.location: Transaction pane, DATA row — label band y219-241, hairline y246, paragraph y256-438

The DATA label and its 'Synthetic demo data' badge sit inside the SAME cell as the transaction identity and the two-line status reason: rules in this pane are at y94, 246, 450, 480, 510, 542, 573, 605, 677, 749, 795, and there is no rule anywhere between the status-reason block (ends y208) and the DATA label (starts y219). The only rule near the label is the 200-grey full-width hairline at y246, which sits BETWEEN the label and the sentences it introduces, 5px below the label against 10px of open whitespace above it. Proximity therefore binds DATA upward to the identity block and fences it off from its own body copy, so nine lines of producer prose (y256-438) read as an unlabelled row. findings.location: Code pane right edge, x638-684 — notice band y165-210 and current-line highlight y371-393
findings.finding: The Code pane's right-edge fade is applied to the whole scroll container rather than to the glyph layer, so it dissolves backgrounds that are not overflowing. The notice band's own grey (221) ramps 221 at x636 to 254 at x684, yet the notice WRAPS — 'Showing from line 26 ... are not in' / 'this window.' — so it has no horizontal overflow at all; a full-width banner that fades out at its right edge reads as a truncated band, which is a false affordance. Worse, the current-line highlight on line 32 (165,243,252) ramps to 245,254,255 over x640-680, so the strongest positional cue in the pane stops 46px short of the pane border and its right terminus is indeterminate. Neither the Call Trace's selected-frame band (full strength 165,243,252 to x1140) nor any pane divider elsewhere is treated this way, so the same highlight primitive terminates two different ways in two panes. Fix: apply the horizontal mask to the text layer only, leaving row backgrounds and banner surfaces full-bleed to the pane border.

findings.location: Transaction pane, FEE PAYER row y605-677 and TARGET row y677-749
findings.finding: 66-character hashes are right-aligned and hard-wrapped into a 287px column, breaking 32 / 32 / 2. Both rows end in a two-character orphan line on a line of its own — '32' at y655-670 and '4c' at y727-742 — each with roughly 270px of white to its left, because right-alignment pushes the orphan to the far edge instead of leaving it beside its parent. The result is two 72px-tall rows whose final third is a two-glyph fragment, in the narrowest column of the page and immediately above the COST row, which also wraps its unit ('mana (FeeJuice)') onto a second right-aligned line. Fix: middle-truncate these to a single line (0x01c8f0...5d932) with the full value available on interaction, or left-align them as a monospace block so the wrap points are even.

findings.location: Call Trace list, frame rows y130-301, x695-800
findings.finding: Depth is carried by exactly one guide rule. Scanning every frame row for vertical ink in x695-800 returns a single column at x706 on all six nested rows, and nothing else: frame text starts at x702 (depth 1, 'main'), x724 (depth 2, 'iterate_asteroids'), x740 (depth 3, 'calculate_damage' and 'status_report') and x756 (depth 4, 'calculate_remaining_shie...'). So depths 3 and 4 are expressed by indentation alone, against B6's requirement of indentation AND a guide, and at depth 4 a reader has no rule to trace back to the parent frame. The indent scale is also not one scale: the first step is 22px (702 to 724) and every subsequent step is 16px (724 to 740 to 756), so the depth-1-to-2 step is 1.4x the others and the ladder is uneven. Fix: one guide per level at a uniform 16px pitch, with the first step brought to 16px too.

findings.location: Identity bar, x370-933
findings.finding: The bar reads as an evenly-spaced strip rather than as groups. Measured object extents and gaps: step pair x370-427, then 16px, pair x444-496, then 16px, pair x513-576, then 16px, pair x593-656, then 16px, scrubber x673-832, then 16px, readout '128' x849-873. The gap that separates one stepping pair from the next is the identical 16px that separates the last stepping pair from the scrubber and the scrubber from the position readout, so 'the stepping controls' is never delimited as a unit from the position machinery. The only stronger separator is 24px (before the first pair at x370, and before the phase rail at x958) — a 1.5x step, too small to register as a level. By contrast the identity cluster on the left is internally spaced at a consistent 8-9px, so the bar has 8px, 16px and 24px doing grouping work with no clear hierarchy between the last two. Fix: keep 16px inside the stepping group and take the group-to-group gap to 32px, so the bar reads as identity / stepping / position / phase / actions.

findings.location: Identity bar left edge x24 versus Code pane title 'CODE' at x13
findings.finding: There is no shared left rail down the page. Every pane insets its title 9px from its own border — 'CODE' at x13 in a pane starting at x4, 'CALL TRACE' at x700 in a pane starting at x691, 'TRANSACTION' at x1158 in a pane starting at x1149 — a consistent 9px. The identity bar's first ink ('the arrow of the demo exit') is at x24, 11px right of 'CODE' and 20px right of the pane edge below it. At laptop width the eye reads a vertical edge down the left of the viewport and the topmost element steps out of it. Fix: bring the identity bar's content inset to 13px so its first glyph aligns with the Code pane's title.

findings.location: Code pane — horizontal mask x638-684 versus vertical mask y870-894
findings.finding: One overflow-fade device is implemented twice with two scales and two scopes, in the same pane. The horizontal ramp is 46px and covers the container (it dims the notice band's grey and the current-line cyan, see finding 4); the vertical ramp is 24-26px and covers content only (pane borders hold 162-grey to y891 and row dividers hold 200-grey to y860, unfaded). A reader cannot learn one meaning for 'fading edge' when its length differs by 1.8x and its subject differs by axis. Fix: settle on a single ramp length (the 46-50px recommended in finding 1) and a single subject (the content layer) for both axes.

findings.location: Code pane line-number gutter x40-80 — lines 26, 48 and 49
findings.finding: The code listing's line pitch is 23px throughout (line-number band centres 266.5, 289.5, 312.5, 336.5, 359.5, ... 734.5) except on three lines where an annotation chip that does not fit inline drops to a half-row and doubles the pitch to 44px: line 26 (centre 222.5 to line 27 at 266.5), line 48 (757.5 to 801.5) and line 49 (801.5 to 845.5). Lines 48 and 49 are consecutive, so an 88px block of the pane carries two code lines. The chips themselves are column-consistent — all four, including line 32's inline '+2', sit on one right rail at x612-637 — so the rail is fine; the cost is 63px of pane height for three chips and a line-number gutter that loses its even rhythm at exactly the point a reader uses it to count lines. Fix: place the wrapped chip on the same 23px row, right-aligned past the fade, rather than opening a second sub-row.

findings.location: Transaction pane, EXECUTIONS note, last two lines (x1157-1430, y874-894)
findings.finding: The new pane-body fade drives body text below the contrast floor BEFORE that text leaves the box. The line 'only proofs, nullifiers and commitments are' occupies y874-885; the pane's inner content edge is y894 and its border y895, so the line has nine clear pixels below it and is not clipped. Its darkest ink ramps monotonically at +7 grey levels per row: 4.54:1 at y875, 3.11:1 at y879, 2.41:1 at y882, 2.22:1 at y883, 2.05:1 at y884 — an x-height mean of 3.11:1 against the 4.5:1 floor for 13px prose. A further line at y892-894 is masked to 1.10:1, present but invisible. This confirms the wide-viewport measurement (2.19-2.22:1) at laptop and worsens it slightly. The text being erased is the producer's own honesty prose, which the brief grades as content rather than decoration; the fade also makes a truncated sentence look like a finished one. The line above it, y856-865, is unmasked at 7.34:1, so the gradient reaches roughly the last 22px of the pane body — which in the Code pane clears line 51 (7.34-9.15:1, unmasked) and only touches the genuinely clipped line 52, and in the Values pane touches nothing (last row 'i / 2 / u32' at 15.5-19:1). The defect is specific to panes whose line-height is shorter than the gradient.

findings.location: Code pane gutter marker column, x75-82: circle-dot at line 32 (y379-387) versus slashed-circle at line 29 (y309-317)
findings.finding: Re-measured independently at this viewport and the previously determined defect holds. Alpha-coverage masks of the two glyphs give IoU 0.781 at threshold 0.5 with only 7 differing pixels out of a 32-pixel union, and total ink of 26.53 versus 30.73 alpha-px — a 14.7% difference on a 28.6 alpha-px mean, smaller than the 23% measured at wide. Every differing pixel lies in the 4x4 interior; the outer ring rows are identical to within 0.06 alpha. At 1x the pair reads as two identical small circles; they separate only by colour here — the slashed circle is neutral #484848 at 9.15:1 on white, the circle-dot is #0E7490 on the #A5F3FC current-line band. That is a use-of-colour dependency for the primary position marker, and it is a different encoding from the dark theme, where both were reported cyan. Separately, the circle-dot's own ring fails as a graphical object: its left and right flanks measure 2.13, 2.23, 2.49, 1.92, 2.71, 1.60, 1.79, 2.40, 2.15, 2.15, 2.40 and 1.96:1 against its band (mean 2.16:1), and only the top and bottom caps reach 3.71-4.29:1. Its area-weighted contrast over a 10x10 cell is 1.39:1. Needs a glyph whose silhouette differs at 1x, and ink at or below #0E5A70.

findings.location: Code pane gutter, x75-82: the per-line coverage dots (lines 27, 28, 31, 34, 37, 41, 42, 44, 46, 48, 50 — e.g. y222-224) versus the current-position circle-dot at line 32
findings.finding: The dot that marks EVERY executed line and the glyph that marks the ONE current line are the same colour in the same 8px-wide column. Coverage dot core is #1A7B95 (26,123,149); the circle-dot's ink is #0E7490 (14,116,144). Same hue (194 vs 193 degrees), three grey levels apart in luminance, indistinguishable side by side. Worse, the circle-dot's interior IS a coverage dot: its centre carries about 2.9 alpha-px of ink against the coverage dot's 3.27 — an 11% difference — so the only thing separating 'you are here' from 'this line ran' is the surrounding ring, and that ring's flanks were measured above at 1.60-2.71:1, below the 3:1 floor for a graphical object. A reader who loses the row band has no reliable second cue. The coverage dot is also weak on its own terms: core 4.87:1 on white but an area-weighted 2.18:1 over its 3x2 lit box and 1.31:1 over its 4x4 cell, with its top row at 2.43:1 — matching the 2.43:1 coverage-dot figure reported at wide. Give the current-position marker a different hue or a filled silhouette, not a ring around the neutral mark.

findings.location: whole view — accent role census: Code pane current-line band (y371-393), Call Trace selected row (y251-275), Code gutter (x75-82), identity bar scrubber (x673-832, y31), iteration chip 3 (x445-478)
findings.finding: The cyan family carries six meanings across five distinct values, and its luminance ordering does not track meaning. #A5F3FC is the Code pane's current-line band AND the Call Trace's selected row — that pairing is correct and is the one cross-pane correspondence the register wants. But #0E7490 is the current-position glyph, #1A7B95 is 'this line executed' (a different concept, and the closest value of all to #0E7490), #155E75 is the scrubber's elapsed portion, and #164E63 is the current loop iteration's numeral and rule. Three separate values encode variants of 'where you are' (#0E7490, #155E75, #164E63) while the fourth concept, coverage, is given the value nearest to the first. A reader cannot learn the family because darker does not mean more current, more selected or more elapsed. Collapse to at most three: one band tint, one position ink, one neutral-hue coverage mark.

findings.location: Code pane header, the 'Iteration 3 of 8' chip strip, x366-678, y99-128
findings.finding: Two problems in one control. Contrast: chips 4-8 (iterations not yet reached) render their numerals as #727272 on the #DDDDDD strip — 3.54:1, below the 4.5:1 floor for 11px text — with anti-aliased strokes falling to 2.35:1 on chip 4 and 1.95:1 on chip 7. Their hairline borders are #A2A2A2 on #DDDDDD at 1.88:1, and the filled chips 1-3 are #919191 on #DDDDDD at 2.32:1; both are below the 3:1 floor for a control boundary, so the chips have no perceivable edge. Semantics: the tone assignment is inverted for a light surface. Chips 1-3 (visited and current) carry a heavy mid-grey FILL that reads as disabled everywhere else in this UI, while chips 4-8 (unreachable from here) are open and white and read as available. This is the clearest evidence that the light theme was derived by flipping the dark one — a raised mid-grey fill signals 'active' on a dark surface and 'inert' on a light one.

findings.location: identity bar — scrubber track (x688-832, y31) versus iteration chips 1-3 (x366-478, y99-128)
findings.finding: #919191 carries two opposite meanings within 300px of each other. In the scrubber it is the UNFILLED remainder of the track — 'not yet reached'. In the iteration strip it is the FILL of chips 1, 2 and 3 — 'already visited, and the current one'. Same value, opposite semantics, both in the top band of the page, both expressing position within the same trace. Compounding it, the scrubber's elapsed segment #155E75 is only 13px of a 160px track, so the eye reads the mid-grey remainder as the dominant mark and the control appears mostly 'filled' at 9.7% progress.

findings.location: all four pane boundaries (borders at y68 and y895; Call Trace/Values split at y561/y566) and the inter-pane gutters at x1145-1148 and x686-690
findings.finding: The light theme's surface levels have collapsed to almost nothing and the entire pane structure rests on one hairline. Page background #ECECEB against the pane surface #FFFFFF is 1.18:1; the pane header band #DDDDDD is 1.36:1; in-pane row rules #C8C8C8 are 1.67:1; status-pill fills #F3F3F3 are 1.11:1. The only element doing structural work is the #A2A2A2 pane border, at 2.55:1 against the pane surface and 2.16:1 against the page — below the 3:1 floor for a boundary, and carrying four panes on its own. Rubric B4's failure case is 'panes distinguished only by a hairline', which is literally the case here. Either drop the pane surface below the page background or take the border to at least #8A8A8A.

findings.location: Code pane current-line band (line 32, y371-393) and Call Trace selected row (calculate_damage, y251-275)
findings.finding: The primary current-position signal in two panes is carried by hue with almost no luminance step. #A5F3FC against the #FFFFFF pane surface is 1.25:1. It is highly visible to normal colour vision because it is saturated, but to a low-vision or monochrome reader the current line and the selected frame are nearly invisible — and per finding 2 the gutter glyph that should be the redundant cue is itself hue-dependent and its ring is under 3:1. In a dark theme the same token carries a real luminance step against the surface; here the inversion left the tint without one. Add a luminance component (a darker band, or a 2-3px left edge rule at 3:1 or better) so position survives without colour.

findings.location: 'Partial' badge (identity bar x206-260, and Transaction pane x1160-1218) versus changed values in the Values pane (9000 at y623-637, 2000 at y790-804) and the 'damage: 0 to 2000' chip in the Code pane

Move the changed-value role out of the warm family, or give the badge a distinctly redder tone.

findings.location: Code pane rows (23 px pitch, y218-873); Call Trace rows (25.3 px pitch, y124-301); Values rows (25 px pitch, y592-860)

findings.location: Code pane, full-width note strip between the file tabs and line 26

findings.location: All four pane headers — CODE (x14,y76), CALL TRACE tab (x931,y76), VALUES (x931,y682), TRANSACTION (x1542,y76)

findings.location: Transaction pane label column x1541 (DATA y200, BLOCK y371, EXECUTIONS y656, DECODED INPUT y796, SELECTOR y823, RAW y849, RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) y986) and Call Trace column head FRAME (x932,y107)
findings.finding: Five structural levels share one rung of the type scale. Pane title, tab label, column head, metadata row label and sub-section label all measure a 9px cap height in tracked uppercase, and only two grey values separate them: #A2A2A2 for titles and column heads, #919191 for row labels. FRAME — a column head inside a pane body — is byte-identical to the pane titles. In the Transaction pane fourteen such labels stack down a 1000px column, and DATA, which the spec calls the pane's premise, differs from the pane's own title by 17 grey levels across that distance, which no reader detects. Raised from r1 #8: the measurement makes this a scale failure rather than the preference I filed it as.

findings.location: Code pane, last visible row — line 61 `println(f"Regenerated {regenerated_shield_as_u32} energy");`, glyph rows y1052–1066
findings.finding: The new bottom fade measures a 24px ramp (y1050–1074) against the listing's 23px line pitch, so it lands on exactly one line and grades the type within a single glyph body: ink falls from 239 at the ascenders to 100 at the baseline, i.e. 12.9:1 at the top of the line and 2.9:1 at the bottom of it. Descenders and the closing `);` are the part that goes. A line of type whose value changes between x-height and baseline reads as a rendering fault, and the residual reading is 'the last line is dim' — which is this pane's existing convention for de-emphasis — rather than 'there is more below'. Confirms in dark what L3/L4 measured in light. Since the ramp cannot be lengthened without worsening the ratio, the fix is positional: mask an inner wrapper and add a half-line of lead so the ramp falls between lines instead of through one.

findings.location: Code pane, gutter column x78-83, line 29 vs line 32
findings.finding: The not-executed marker and the current-position marker are separated by hue alone. And the grey used for the not-executed state is #919191, the page's generic muted tone (line numbers, metadata labels, the inactive EVENT LOG tab, all eight control icons, chip labels, 'By call order.'), so it does not read as a state colour at all. findings.location: page-wide: identity-bar scrubber x673-696; iteration chip x503-566 y105-121; Code pane current-line rail x5-8 y352-374 and line number x47-64; Code gutter dots x78-79; Call Trace selected-frame rail x922-923 y251-276; Code pane type tokens (Field, u32)

findings.location: Code pane, last line (line 61) at y1051-1066 and its coverage dot at x78-79 y1058-1059; pane bottom border at y1075
findings.finding: The new bottom fade pushes text below the contrast floor while that text is still entirely inside the box. Measured on the RAW block's flat surface, the mask is a 24px linear alpha ramp: 1.00 at y=1050 falling to 0.04 at y=1074. Line 61 spans y1051-1066, nine pixels clear of the pane border, and it is the LAST rendered line - there is no ink at all between y=1067 and the border, so the fade is not softening a cut edge, it is dimming a complete line for nothing. The line-61 coverage dot measures 2.43:1 on its upper row and 3.62:1 on its lower, against 6.86:1 for the identical dot on line 60 - the fade halves a state marker that has no redundant encoding. This confirms the light-theme lens's 2.19-2.22:1 and 2.43:1 to two decimals in dark. The mask should stop at the last full line box, or exempt gutter marker glyphs.

findings.location: Transaction pane, RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) code block, x1543-1906 y1009-1075
findings.finding: Confirmed in dark: masking the pane body fades the RAW block's own surface and erases its bottom boundary. The block is separated from the pane by a tone step only - #000000 against #1b1b1b, 1.22:1, with no border - and the bottom fade lifts it to #191919 by y=1073, i.e. 1.02:1 against the pane. The block's bottom edge and its two bottom rounded corners are gone; a 46px horizontal fade does the same to its right edge (x1859 to x1905). findings.location: identity bar, phase rail at x≈958-1205, and the empty gap at x≈833-855 between the scrubber and the 128 / 1315 readout where the engine status renders at 1920
findings.finding: The phase rail is the only carrier of the fetching state at this viewport, and at this viewport it is unlabelled. At 1920 the bar renders 'Engine loading - 18 MB' between the scrubber and the position readout; at 1440 that phrase is dropped and the gap is empty, so three chips - FETCHING, OPENING, POSITIONING - stand with no subject. The rail therefore asserts an unfinished phase about an object the reader cannot identify, and its terminal chip POSITIONING names precisely what the panes visibly already did: current line 32 highlighted in Code, frame six selected in Call Trace, ten values at step N, 128 / 1315 on the scrubber. Both facts are true, but the noun that keeps them from colliding was deleted by the responsive rule, leaving only two readings, both wrong: the rail is stale, or the populated panes are a skeleton. The inert controls cannot join them either - stepping glyphs are #565656, the same ink as the not-yet-reached OPENING and POSITIONING chips, so 'cannot act' and 'has not happened yet' are one grey. findings.location: Identity bar, phase rail at x≈960–1200, y≈18–42 — immediately right of the `128 / 1315` position readout

The charitable reading is that this is a statically rendered session with the replay engine still loading behind it, which this register explicitly permits; but the expectation block says that state is carried by three devices together — the phase rail, the controls' own status, and the buttons' disabled state — and only one of the three is firing. All eight stepping glyphs render at a uniform #919191 with no disabled treatment, and no controls status text appears anywhere in the bar. So the rail is either wrong about the engine or unsupported by the two elements sitting 500px to its left. It is the weakest element because it is the page's single dedicated state indicator, it is the only thing on the surface asserting something the rest of the surface contradicts, and a status device that cannot be told apart from a not-yet-loaded session is reporting nothing. Named phases are the right primitive; the active-phase mark has to land on the phase the panes are actually showing, and the controls have to agree with it.

findings.location: all four panes — pane titles CODE (x10,y81), VALUES (x707,y579), TRANSACTION (x1157,y81); call-trace column header FRAME (x700,y107); transaction row labels DATA (x1157,y227), BLOCK (y463), TYPE (y494), EXECUTIONS (y808)

findings.location: identity bar position readout (x849–933, y31) versus call-trace 'main' row opcode count (x1100, y138); also Values pane value column (x940–1030) and COST · MANA (x1290, y762)

findings.location: Transaction pane, DATA row provenance note (x1157–1428, y251–444)

findings.location: Code pane gutter, execution column at x≈78 — line 29 ⊘ (y313), line 32 ⊙ (y383), executed-line dots on lines 26, 27, 28, 31

findings.location: Code pane, line-number column — line 26→27 (y224→267), 48→49 (y758→802), 49→50 (y802→843) against lines 28–39

findings.location: Code pane, loop strip (y 105-125): `LOOP iterate_asteroids` at x 20-175, `line 4` at x 180-215, `Iteration 3 of 8` at x 222-360

findings.location: Call Trace opcode column, `1,315` (x 1480-1518, y 137) and `1,208` (y 162), against COST · MANA in the Transaction pane, `88000 / 200000` (x 1685-1790, y 633)

findings.location: Code pane listing, rows 26-27 (glyph bands y 198-212 and y 241-256, with a chip row at y 216-234) and rows 47-49 (y 712, 749, 780)

findings.location: Tabbed navigation region (x 922-1526, y 68-668): content ends at the `By call order.` footer at y ~325; measured blank from y 325 to y 668

findings.location: Code pane, notice strip at y 178: `Showing from line 26 — the session's position is below, and the lines above it are not in this window.`
findings.finding: Unchanged. findings.location: Values pane, `masses` (x 931, y 781-794) and `masses[2]` (x 939, y 807-819)

findings.location: Code pane gutter, x 76-84: the not-taken mark on line 29 (y 295) and the current/taken mark on line 32 (y 364), against the plain steppable dots on lines 26-28 and 31

Differentiating them at the outline — a filled disc against an open ring — would resolve it without a size increase.

findings.location: Four selection strips: region tabs (y 81), iteration chips (y 114), file tabs (y 146), phase rail (x 1225-1480, y 31)
findings.finding: Unchanged. The page expresses 'one selected among a set' four different ways within 150px of vertical space: uppercase sans with a heavy underline; a filled grey box with a coloured numeral and a double underline; monospace with a short rounded underline; and uppercase inside a tinted pill segment. findings.location: Transaction pane: the dashes on `SELECTOR` (x 1897-1905, y 829-830) and `RAW` (y 854-855), against the `No timestamp published` pill on AGE (y 439) and the `Not observable` pill on EXECUTIONS private (y 687)

findings.location: Identity bar `0xb63616…6359` (x 86-196, y 31); Transaction pane header `0xb636167a…66d46359` (y 111) and the full hash wrapped across y 137-155; FEE PAYER (y 535-556) and TARGET (y 585-607)

findings.location: navigation column (x921-1529): Call Trace tabbed region below the 'By call order.' footer at y320, and the Values pane below its last row at y952
findings.finding: Re-measured and the prior finding holds unchanged. The tabbed region is 347px empty (y320 to its inner bottom edge y667) = 57.8% of its 600px; Values is 121px empty (y952 to y1073) = 30.3% of its 399px. Take width from the nav column and give it to Code.

findings.location: Code pane, the row after line 26 (y205-249) and the row after line 48 (y736-780)
findings.finding: The code listing runs a 23px line pitch for 34 of its 36 rows, and breaks to 44px at exactly two: the rows where the overflow chips '+3' (x844-867, cy225) and '+2' (cy759) wrap below the code instead of sitting inline. Two consequences. First, the gutter shows an unexplained double-height gap after lines 26 and 48, so screen rows stop corresponding to source lines. Second, each wrapped chip lands almost exactly equidistant between the two lines it sits between ('+3' is 20px below line 26 and 24px above line 27), so proximity gives no cue which line it annotates — the inline chips that do fit (damage=0, cy250) are baseline-exact on their line, which makes the wrapped ones read as belonging to neither. Right-align the wrapped chip inside its own line's box, or clip it to the line height.

findings.location: Call Trace list, x936, rows 2-7 (y153-300)
findings.finding: Exactly one depth guide is drawn, at x936, and it is drawn at that same x on every non-root row regardless of depth. The label ladder is 932 (depth 0) / 954 / 970 / 986, so depth 2 and depth 3 rows carry indentation alone with a guide that marks depth 1's channel, not their own — a fixed tick that means 'not root' rather than 'this deep'. The ladder is also not one step: 932 to 954 is 22px, then 16px per level thereafter, so the first indent is 6px off the scale the rest of the ladder uses. Draw one guide per ancestor level and make the first step 16px like the others.

findings.location: Transaction pane, DATA row: label and 'Synthetic demo data' badge at y196-215, hairline at y224, provenance sentences beginning y232
findings.finding: The row's hairline falls BELOW the DATA label instead of above it, so proximity groups the label with the wrong content. The gap from the 'succeeded' status-reason line down to the DATA label is 19px with no rule between them; the gap from the label down to the sentences it heads is 22px AND crosses a rule. Read literally, the pane's row grid puts the identity block (Partial badge, full hash, status reason) and the DATA label in one cell y95-224, and leaves the producer's sentences in an unlabelled cell y225-363. Since the brief's own concern is that this row may be too quiet for the claim it makes, having its label visually annexed by the block above it is the layout half of that problem. Move the rule above the DATA label.

findings.location: all pane bodies, bottom edge — measured in the Code pane at y1046-1072 and the Transaction pane RAW block at y1049-1073
findings.finding: The new vertical fade succeeds: it reads as 'there is more below', not as a clip. The disambiguator is that the whole row fades including the line-number gutter, which a syntax colour could not do, and in the Transaction pane the RAW block's own grey background fades out with its text so the box is open at the bottom rather than cut. But it is not the same fade turned ninety degrees: extrapolating the mask from the rendered glyph luminance, the vertical ramp spans ~26px (alpha 1.0 at y1046 to 0 at y1072) while the horizontal ramp in the SAME pane spans ~48px (x868 to x915). At a 23px line pitch a 26px ramp admits exactly one line, which is why the effect is weakest in the Transaction pane where that one line is low-contrast grey-on-grey. Lengthen the vertical ramp to the horizontal's ~48px and a second, nearly-gone line enters the fade.

findings.location: identity bar, x370-1203
findings.finding: Grouping is carried by proximity only in the left third. The identity cluster is internally 8-9px ('demo' 24-75, hash 85-193, Partial 202-261, 'block' 271-305, '101' 315-335) and separated from what follows by 24px at the divider. The bar already owns a 24px group separator — use it around the control block, as it is used before the phase rail (1203-1228).

findings.location: pane grid gutters: column gutter x917-920 (Code to nav, nav to Transaction), row gutter y669-674 (tabbed region to Values)
findings.finding: The pane grid uses two different gutter values on its two axes: 4px between columns and 6px between rows. The page margin is 4px on all four edges. Neither 4 nor 6 is on the 8/16/24 scale the identity bar uses. The 2px difference is not visible in isolation but it means the grid has no single gutter token; pick one value for both axes.

findings.location: Code pane, file-tab row (Nargo.toml / Prover.toml / src/main.nr / src/shield.nr) at y136-158

findings.location: Transaction pane metadata rows, AGE / CANONICAL / FINALITY (rules at y423, 455, 487, 518)
findings.finding: Rows whose value is a pill are taller than rows whose value is plain text: BLOCK and TYPE are 30px (y363-393, y393-423) and COST-MANA is 30px (y620-650), while AGE is 32px, CANONICAL 32px and FINALITY 31px. findings.location: Code pane, last line (61) at y1052-1066; Transaction pane, `"aztec": {` row at y1049-1062
findings.finding: The new bottom fade pushes a complete, unclipped line below the contrast floor while it is still fully inside the pane. Measured on the constant-ink line-number column, line 61 runs #6F6F6F (5.02:1) at the glyph top to #AEAEAE (2.22:1) at the glyph bottom, i.e. alpha 0.85 -> 0.48; its code text runs 4.81:1 -> 2.19:1. Glyph bottoms sit 12px clear of the pane border at y1075. Same in the Transaction pane: 13.13:1 -> 3.04:1, ending 13px above the border. The ramp measures ~29px against a 23px line pitch, so it can never soften only the clipped sliver — it always consumes one whole readable row. Fix: hold alpha at 1.0 for the first ~12px of the ramp and fade only the final 10-12px, so the last fully-rendered line stays above 4.5:1.

findings.location: Transaction pane, RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) inset code block, y1048-1074
findings.finding: The mask is applied to the pane body, not to the ink, so it erases surface levels as well as text. The inset block's own background is washed from #ECECEB to #F0F0EF by y1055, #F7F7F7 by y1064 and #FBFBFB by y1074 — the block loses its container tone and its bottom boundary entirely. The reversal is the damaging part: the page canvas immediately below the pane border is #ECECEB, darker than the faded block above it, so the surface gets lighter approaching the edge and then abruptly darker past it, which reads as the block ending rather than continuing — the opposite of what the fade was added to say. Fix: scope the mask to the scrolling content layer, or composite the gradient toward the block's own #ECECEB rather than toward transparent.

findings.location: Code pane gutter, coverage mark for line 61 at x78-79, y1058-1060
findings.finding: The fade extinguishes a state marker while it is still inside the pane. Line 61's coverage dot renders at #74AFBF / #6BAABA = 2.43:1 and 2.60:1 against white, where the other eighteen dots all measure 4.87:1 (core #1A7B95). It is a 2x2px graphical mark 15px above the pane border and now sits below the 3:1 non-text floor, so a reader scanning the coverage column reads line 61 as having no coverage — a state rendered as a different state. Not P1 only because the affected row is the one the reader is about to scroll past. Fixed by finding 1's shorter ramp, but worth verifying separately: small marks lose legibility to a mask far faster than glyph strokes do.

findings.location: Code pane header, loop-iteration strip, pill `3` at x508-564, y100-128
findings.finding: The current loop iteration is the faintest item in its own strip. Pill 3's digit and its underline are #164E63 on the #919191 pill fill = 2.89:1, while the non-current past pills `1` and `2` carry #242424 on the identical fill at 4.93:1. The single digit that says which of eight iterations you are looking at is 1.7x fainter than its neighbours, and its cyan underline — the only other cue — measures the same 2.89:1, below the 3:1 non-text floor. Contrast hierarchy is inverted against importance. Fix: keep the cyan as the identity cue but raise it to at least #0E7490 on a lighter selected fill, or invert the pill (dark fill, #FFFFFF digit) so the current iteration is the highest-contrast, not the lowest.

findings.location: Code pane header, loop-iteration strip, pills `4`-`8` at x576-904, y100-128
findings.finding: Future-iteration digits sit below the small-text floor. Pills 4, 5 and 8 measure #727272-#747474 on #DDDDDD = 3.44-3.54:1 at the darkest stroke core, and 2.64-3.30:1 across the bulk of the antialiased stroke, at roughly 11px. This is the page's only remaining not-yet-reached / disabled-ish treatment and it was set by lightening the ink rather than by choosing a pair. Fix: keep the #DDDDDD fill and set the digit to #565656 (5.40:1 on that fill), which still reads as recessed against the #242424 of the executed pills.

findings.location: Identity bar scrubber (y26-38) versus the iteration strip directly below it (y100-128)
findings.finding: The token #919191 carries opposite meanings 60px apart in the same visual band. On the scrubber it is the UNREACHED remainder: the #155E75 elapsed fill runs x673-696 and the grey runs x697-932, i.e. 9.2% filled for step 128/1315. On the iteration strip immediately below, #919191 fills iterations 1-3 — the ones ALREADY EXECUTED — with #DDDDDD for the unreached 4-8. Two progress indicators, one grey, inverted semantics. Fix: pick one direction for 'consumed' and use the same fill for both; the scrubber's #155E75 elapsed / #919191 remaining is the more conventional pair, so the iteration strip should invert.

findings.location: Whole frame — Code gutter x72-90, Code line band y352-374, Call Trace selected row y255-273, scrubber x673-696, iteration pill 3, and the `Field`/`u32` tokens throughout the Code pane
findings.finding: Cyan carries five distinct meanings across four tokens, with two exact-hex collisions. Full-frame census: #A5F3FC (26,286px), #0E7490, #155E75 (994px), #164E63 (278px), covering (1) current position — Code line band, Call Trace selected row and left rail, correctly one token in both panes; (2) trace coverage — nineteen `·` marks; (3) scrubber elapsed; (4) selected loop iteration; (5) the `Field` and `u32` type tokens in the editor palette. Collision A: the ⊙ current-position marker and the `·` coverage marks are the SAME token — the dot core #1A7B95 solves to #0E7490 at alpha 0.95 over white, and the ring core is #0E7490 at alpha 1.0. Collision B: the scrubber's elapsed fill and the `Field`/`u32` type tokens are both exactly #155E75. Fix: reserve the cyan family for position alone and move coverage to a neutral, which also resolves finding 8.

findings.location: Code pane gutter — ⊘ at x75-82/y291-299, ⊙ at x75-82/y360-368, `·` marks at x78-79 on nineteen rows
findings.finding: Re-measured independently; confirming the recorded defect and revising my own round-1 conclusion. ⊘ core #484848 on #FFFFFF = 9.15:1. ⊙ core #0E7490 on the #A5F3FC band = 4.29:1, but only 4 of the ring's 24 ink pixels reach it — the flanks measure 3.91, 2.71, 2.13 and 1.69:1, so most of the ring is under the 3:1 non-text floor, which reproduces the other lens's 2.40/2.23 flank finding. Greyscaled, the ⊙ core is 107/255 and the `·` core is 113/255 — a 6-value difference, so without colour the current-position marker and a coverage mark have effectively identical ink and are separated only by size (7x8px ring vs 2x2px square). Against ⊘, ⊙ carries 123 units of ink-vs-local-background to ⊘'s 183, a 33% deficit. I withdraw 'distinguishable with zero margin' and join the majority: not reliably distinguishable without colour. No new fix implied beyond the pending glyph redesign; recording the measurement so the redesign has a target — give ⊙ an achromatic ring at ≥3:1 on the band and let the interior dot, not the hue, carry the meaning.

findings.location: Identity bar `FETCHING` chip (x1234-1300, y22-42) and Transaction pane `Synthetic demo data` badge (x1760-1905, y198-220)

The tone does not contradict the label — informational blue is right for 'synthetic' — so this is not the P1 the presence check guards. But the provenance row is the one thing on this page graded as content rather than chrome, and it currently wears the same colour as a chip that disappears in a second. Fix: give the provenance badge its own tone (a neutral-slate or a distinct violet) so the page's single honesty claim is not a member of the loading-state palette.

findings.location: Identity bar phase rail, x1228-1476, y20-44
findings.finding: The rail's active state is carried by colour alone. Active `FETCHING` is #1E40AF on #DBEAFE = 7.15:1; inactive `OPENING` and `POSITIONING` are #565656 on #FFFFFF = 7.34:1 — the inactive chips are marginally HIGHER contrast than the active one. Greyscaled the rail has no active state at all, which matters because the rail is one of the two things the brief says must carry the engine's loading state. findings.location: Transaction pane, `SELECTOR` and `RAW` rows, value column at x1890-1906, y820-865
findings.finding: The new em dash placeholder sits below the text floor. It renders at #8A8A8A on #FFFFFF = 3.45:1, against #565656 / 7.34:1 for the `SELECTOR` and `RAW` labels on the same rows, and at 1-2px stroke weight it is close enough to the #C8C8C8 row rules to be taken for one. findings.location: Code pane, the four stacked bands from y69 to y191
findings.finding: #DDDDDD is the only non-white surface step in the Code pane and it carries four roles plus a fifth: pane header band (y69-98), LOOP context row (y100-127), file-tab strip (y129-159), the `Showing from line 26...` window notice (y165-191), and the inline value chips (`damage=0`, `+3`, `damage: 0->2000`). The result is 123px of one grey at the top of the pane, and the divider weights do not track the hierarchy: the strong #A2A2A2 (2.55:1) separates the LOOP row from the tab strip, which are peers, while the weak #C8C8C8 (1.67:1) separates the notice — the only one of the four that is a message rather than chrome — from the code body. findings.location: Code pane — function names throughout versus the `damage: 0->2000` chip at x490-600/y352-372 and the changed values and accent bars in the Values pane at x920-1410
findings.finding: The warm end of the palette doubles up. Function names in the editor palette are #713F12 (hue 28deg) and the changed-value role — the inline diff chip, the `9000`/`2000` values and the left accent bars — is #854D0E (hue 32deg); at 11px on a single code line the two are indistinguishable, so 'this is a function' and 'this value changed at this step' share a colour. Two smaller instances: source comments and the `Trace ready` badge text are both exactly #166534, and numeric literals (#6D28D9) sit 20deg from the link indigo (#4F46E5), with the `line 4` link and the literal `100` fifteen rows apart in the same pane. findings.location: all pane bodies; measurable at Transaction pane RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) block y1051-1074 and Code pane line 61 y1052-1066
findings.finding: The new bottom fade ramp is 24px, exactly one 23px line-height, so it attenuates exactly one line: the RAW block's last line goes from ink 36 at its cap-height to 141 at its baseline while the line above stays at full contrast. A fade reads as 'there is more' when the eye sees a progression across two or three successive lines at descending opacity; across one line it reads as 'the last line is dim'. The same design system already fades horizontally over ~30px, which at 8.2px per mono character is ~3.7 characters of content (Code pane line 40, ink 93 at x880 washing to 194 at x902) - the vertical ramp should match that ratio at ~50-56px, i.e. two to two-and-a-half line-heights. Verdict on the change: the mid-glyph cut the five reviewers reported is genuinely gone and no glyph is now sliced by a border, but the continuation signal is not yet unambiguous.

findings.location: Transaction pane, RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) block, y1026-1074
findings.finding: The fade is the only overflow cue on the page - no scrollbar track or gutter is rendered in any pane body. The block shows two lines ('{' and '"aztec": {') of a JSON payload of unknown size, so a reader cannot tell whether two lines or two hundred are below. This product quantifies elsewhere (AGE says 'No timestamp published', the identity bar says 'Engine loading - 18 MB'); the RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) heading should carry a line or byte count so the fade announces a measured quantity rather than an unmeasured one.

findings.location: middle column (x926-1523) Call Trace region y68-669, against Transaction pane x1538-1910
findings.finding: Re-measured this round and unchanged: the Call Trace region is 601px tall, its seven frames plus the 'By call order.' footer end at y328, leaving 341px empty - 56.7% of the region and 59.4% of the 574px below the tab strip. Values below it is 401px with its last rule at y952, 123px empty (30.7%). The widest frame row ('calculate_remaining_shield_pct zk_shields - src/shield.nr') ends at x1353 and the right-aligned opcode column starts at x1506, a 153px dead band; the widest Values row ('masses') has 147px between the label end at x1004 and the array's left edge at x1151. So the 598px middle column can give up 120-130px of width with no row in either pane losing content, while the 373px Transaction pane beside it now visibly fades content off its bottom edge. The fade did not change this arithmetic - it only made the shortage advertise itself, which makes a visible shortage sit next to a visible 341px surplus.

findings.location: Transaction pane, full column x1538-1910, y205-1074
findings.finding: Section headings (DATA y205, EXECUTIONS y663, DECODED INPUT y805) and row labels (BLOCK y376, TYPE, AGE, CANONICAL, FINALITY, FEE PAYER, TARGET, COST - MANA y633, SELECTOR y828, RAW y853) share one type treatment: 9px cap-height letterspaced small-caps, same weight, same grey. findings.location: Not observable card (x 503-1204) against the Overview grid and Raw block (x 503-1414)
